---
title: "019 — Diátaxis docs website"
---

> **Status:** standing

**Goal.** Restructure the documentation around the Diátaxis framework — tutorials,
how-to guides, reference, explanation — published as a browsable website instead of a
linear book, because the book forced task-hunters and fact-hunters through one fixed
sequence with teaching, task, and reference material interleaved. The idea→spec
relationship runs from ideas/006-diataxis-docs into spec 019-diataxis-docs-website: the
verdict chose the owner's own card — flip `_quarto.yml` from `book` to `website` and
re-home every page into exactly one quadrant, with non-Diátaxis content (developer notes,
decision history, changelog) on dedicated shelves rather than squeezed into Explanation.
The runner-up rulings matter as much: the book-with-relabels card was rejected as a
half-measure ("seems lazy" — it kept linear prev/next chrome), and the docs-platform card
(a Docusaurus/MkDocs-class migration) was declined outright — a full content migration
plus a permanent second toolchain for versioning and generated-reference features that pay
off only if the docs keep growing. Revisit a platform only then.

**Why.** The craving recorded at verdict time was organization plus website feel *now*.
Readers arrive with different intents — learn, do, look up — and quadrant-shaped
navigation plus website chrome shorten every journey because the sidebar can say which
section serves which. Staying in Quarto kept the GitHub Pages pipeline, search, and every
toolchain pin untouched, so the entire risk budget went to content surgery and link
continuity instead of platform migration.

**Outcome & reversals.** Landed 2026-09-04 (all 27 tasks checked) and shipped in 0.6.0:
quadrant directories (`tutorials/`, `how-to/`, `reference/`, `explanation/`) plus
`dev-notes/` and `history/` shelves; an intent-based landing page stating what each
section is for; one sidebar grouped by section, with website chrome replacing book
pagination. Page splitting stayed "3/4 strict" per the owner ruling — split where a page
genuinely interleaves walkthrough and reference, tolerate minor mixing; quadrant purity is
not a goal in itself. Link continuity was repaired in the same cutover rather than
deferred: every moved page gained Quarto `aliases` (emitted as redirect pages, so old deep
links survive on static hosting), and repository-level doc-path pointers — `AGENTS.md`,
`CONTRIBUTING.md`/`README.md`, and the constitution's authoritative-design citations —
were updated together, the constitution via a PATCH-level amendment with a Sync Impact
Report. An automated `lychee` check over the rendered site reached zero broken internal
links, and the publish workflow stayed byte-identical — same destination, same pipeline.
No reversals; the accepted standing cost was on the record from the idea stage: nothing in
the format enforces where new pages land, so the sidebar stays honest only as long as
per-page filing does. The decision history itself — this document — is one of the
dedicated shelves the restructure declared.

**Learnings.**

- An afternoon of configuration beats a platform migration when the craving is
  organization rather than features.
- Aliases turn URL churn from a lingering hazard into a solved one — free on static
  hosting, so broken deep links have no excuse.
- Doc-path references in governance documents are load-bearing: a cutover must repair
  agent instructions and the constitution in the same change or they silently rot.
- Taxonomy orphans — chronological dev notes, decision history — deserve declared
  shelves, not unprincipled exceptions squeezed into a quadrant.
